common_name: Vancouver Centennial Pelargonium (Bronze Star-Leaf Fancy Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates. Vancouver Centennial is grown chiefly for its striking foliage rather than heavy bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Vancouver Centennial is a stellar-type fancy-leaf pelargonium with small, deeply cut, star-shaped leaves marked by a bold bronze-maroon central zone against a bright chartreuse-gold background, a striking two-tone foliage pattern that provides season-long interest even between the modest clusters of small orange-red flowers. Its compact, mounding habit and small scale make it well suited to containers, window boxes, and the front of a border where its detailed leaf pattern can be appreciated up close. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Mrs. Pollock Pelargonium (Classic Tricolor Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates. Mrs. Pollock's tricolor leaf pattern is most vivid in bright light.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Mrs. Pollock is a Victorian-era tricolor zonal geranium, one of the oldest and most famous fancy-leaf pelargonium cultivars still grown, with rounded leaves marked in bands of gold, deep bronze-red, and green that shift and deepen through the season, topped with small orange-red flowers that are secondary to the dramatic foliage display. Its long garden history and bold, old-fashioned color combination make it a favorite for heritage and cottage-style plantings. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Mabel Grey is widely considered the most intensely and purely lemon-scented of all the scented geraniums, its deeply cut, rough-textured, sharply pointed leaves releasing a strong citrus fragrance at the lightest touch, far more potent than milder lemon-scented cultivars. Small lavender-pink flowers appear but are incidental to the plant's main appeal as a fragrance and culinary herb; the leaves can flavor teas, baked goods, and sugars, or be crushed and rubbed on skin as a natural citrus-scented insect deterrent. Pinch stems to keep it bushy and encourage fuller growth, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.
